history.period: 1921 (per a local/secondary account; verify - the district tourism page gives no date)
history.summary: A Shiva hilltop temple on the Badheimunda hills, Kali Mandir Road, Jharsuguda, from which the whole city is visible. The district tourism page places it on a small hill ~3 km from the railway station and ~3.5 km from the bus stand, with worship dedicated to Lord Shiva; other sources give varying distances (1 km, 2 km, 5 km - flag the inconsistency). A secondary local account says it was built in 1921 by Gujarati contractor Sri Bitthal Bhai Saha, covers ~2000 sq ft, stands ~20 ft tall in orange/yellow, and is reached by 66 steps plus a motorable road. It narrates that saint Mahant Nand Kishor Puri of Chitrotpala Math meditated here, the temple was neglected after his death, and a local committee revived it in 1921. An adjacent Hanuman temple exists, and the district's tallest temple flag (128 ft) is claimed for it. CONFLICT FLAG: reported hours are 5:00 AM-8:30 PM (findglocal) vs 6:00 AM-10:00 PM (place listing); verify locally.

name: Pahadi Mandir
town_description: Jharsuguda is the industrial 'powerhouse of Odisha' in the west of the state, with its own airport (Veer Surendra Sai Airport) and a major railway junction. The Pahadi Mandir sits on the Badheimunda hill off Kali Mandir Road, offering a view of the whole city; coordinates are from its mapped place listing.
